findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` handler only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. Since `cacheUpdatedAt` shown in the dropdown comes from the `connectedCalendars` query result, after a user deletes the cache the UI will keep showing the old 'Cache Status'/timestamp until an unrelated refetch happens. This defeats the core purpose of the feature (showing accurate cache status) and matches the review checklist item 'Confirm cache deletion works and UI updates appropriately', which this implementation does not satisfy.

findings.title: deleteCache handler throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: `deleteCacheHandler` throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError` with a proper code (e.g. `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`) as is the convention elsewhere in the tRPC routers in this codebase. This results in a generic 500 Internal Server Error being surfaced to the client/monitoring instead of a meaningful 4xx error, which complicates error tracking/alerting and is inconsistent with how access-denied/not-found cases are handled by other handlers.

findings.title: Credential existence check fetches full credential row including secrets
findings.body: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` has no `select` clause, so it loads the entire Credential record into memory, including the `key` field which typically stores OAuth tokens/secrets. Since only an existence/ownership check is needed here, this unnecessarily pulls sensitive data into the handler's memory/log context (e.g. via error reporting middleware) when a `select: { id: true }` would suffice.

findings.title: dev:cron script switched to npx tsx without declaring tsx as a dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not added to `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` remains listed). Using `npx` will attempt to fetch/install `tsx` on demand, which can fail in offline/CI/Yarn PnP environments and is inconsistent with the rest of the monorepo's tooling (other scripts in the same file still use `ts-node` directly). The dependency should be added explicitly and invoked via the existing package manager instead of `npx`.

findings.title: New helper script uses macOS-only sed syntax, will fail on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS form of `sed -i` which requires an empty string argument for in-place editing without backup. On GNU/Linux (the typical CI/dev container OS), this syntax is invalid and will either error out or behave unexpectedly, making this new developer utility script non-portable despite being added to a cross-platform repo.

findings.title: Handler bypasses the CalendarCache factory/feature-flag pattern used elsewhere
findings.body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` directly instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` to call `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the established factory used throughout the codebase to decide between the real repository and `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (e.g. based on the 'calendar-cache' feature flag/license gating). As a result, cache status is always read directly from the database regardless of whether calendar caching is enabled for the user's team/org, which is inconsistent with how caching is gated everywhere else and could surface stale/irrelevant cache status data for users whose org has calendar caching disabled.

findings.title: Unconditional broad SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update with no consumer, flagged by the PR author as unresolved
findings.body: After every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` call, `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` updates `updatedAt` for ALL selected calendars under the credential, not just the subset that was actually refreshed in that call (the per-event-type grouping is bypassed). The PR description itself notes this field is not currently surfaced in the UI (the feature uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt` instead) and asks whether this update should be removed. Shipping this as-is adds extra, seemingly unused database writes on every cache refresh cycle and risks future confusion/misuse of a timestamp that doesn't actually reflect per-calendar freshness.

findings.title: Backfilled updatedAt for existing CalendarCache rows will misrepresent cache freshness
findings.body: The migration adds `updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`, which backfills all pre-existing CalendarCache rows with the migration deployment timestamp rather than their actual last-updated time. Once deployed, the new 'Cache Status'/'Last updated' UI will show every pre-existing cache entry as having been refreshed at the exact moment of deployment, which is misleading to users trying to judge actual cache freshness until those rows are naturally re-upserted.

findings.title: No tests added for new deleteCache handler, cache status repository method, or UI component
findings.body: This PR introduces several new pieces of logic (`deleteCacheHandler`, `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, and the `CredentialActionsDropdown` component) with user-facing destructive actions (cache deletion) and access-control checks, but no unit or integration tests were added for any of them. The PR's own review checklist calls out multiple untested behaviors (authorization, cache status mapping, conditional rendering) as high priority items needing manual verification, which should instead be covered by automated tests before merge.
